sections.h2: Who sends and collects property tax in Fayette County?
sections.html:
The Fayette County Tax Commissioner mails the bills and takes the payments, and the Assessors' Office values the property. The assessors' own page says plainly that it does not generate tax bills, and it sends billing questions to the commissioner at 770-461-3652.

The Tax Commissioner works from the county administrative complex at 140 W. Stonewall Avenue in Fayetteville. Suite 110 handles property tax and mobile homes, and Suite 109 handles motor vehicles. The mailing address is P.O. Box 70, Fayetteville, GA 30214. Property tax and mobile home hours are Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and a pay-by-phone line, (770) 800-6273, is listed for payments.

City tax is not billed separately. The commissioner's FAQ says all city taxes are on the county bill and the county passes the city share to Fayetteville, Peachtree City, Tyrone, Brooks or Woolsey.

sections.h2: What is the Fayette County property tax calendar?
sections.html:
Bills go out in the fall, and the commissioner's FAQ says taxpayers are given 60 days from the date the original bills were mailed. The table lists the dates the commissioner publishes.

Fayette County property tax dates (source: Tax Commissioner FAQ)
ItemDate or rule
Return of property valueJanuary 1 to April 1
Regular homestead applicationYear round, but complete by April 1 for that tax year
Mobile home billsMailed January 1, due on or before April 1, 10 percent penalty after the due date
Real property billsExpected around mid September
DelinquencyAfter November 15, or 60 days after mailing if that is later

Interest accrues once the bill is delinquent. The commissioner reminds owners that a missing bill does not excuse the debt: it is the owner's duty to ask the office for the amount due before the delinquent date. Bills are not sent to a mortgage company unless the lender requests a copy, so give your servicer the lower portion of your bill and include the loan number.

sections.h2: How does the Fayette County homestead exemption work?
sections.html:
Fayette residents who own and occupy a home on January 1 can claim a regular homestead exemption. The commissioner's FAQ prints the amounts as the first $2,000 of assessed value on the school portion and $5,000 on the county portion of the bill. Homestead is limited to one property, which must be your primary residence.

  • Applications can be made year round and must be complete by April 1 to apply to the current tax year.
  • The assessors' page says taxpayers may also apply beyond the old April 1 date, up to the end of the 45-day appeal window on their assessment notice.
  • Once granted, the exemption continues each year at the same address.
  • Someone who qualified for the age 62 exemption must still apply separately when reaching 65.
  • Mobile home residents are not eligible for homestead.

The assessors' page adds that its office also processes homestead applications, so ask which counter takes the form before you go.

sections.h2: What are the floating homestead exemptions in Fayette County?
sections.html:
Fayette voters approved House Bill 1166 in November 2020, an extra homestead exemption that applies to the school board portion of the bill. A similar measure, House Bill 581, was approved by voters in November 2024 and applies to every taxing entity except bonds.

The county's news page says the Fayette County school board opted out of HB 581 in favor of the existing HB 1166 exemption. Both are floating exemptions, so the amount depends on the gap between the current value and a base year value. Ask the Assessors' Office which base year applies to your parcel.

That detail matters when you sell. Buyers who ask what the property tax will be should hear that your bill reflects your own exemption status, and that they need to apply for theirs after closing.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Fayette County assessment?
sections.html:
An appeal must be sent to the Board of Tax Assessors and postmarked within 45 days of the mailing date on the notice of assessment, according to the Department of Revenue. The assessors' page shows how this played out in 2026: commercial and residential notices were mailed June 23, and personal property notices were mailed July 28.

If the assessors do not agree with your appeal, the dispute can go to the county Board of Equalization. The Clerk of Superior Court manages that board's records, notices and decision letters. A further appeal goes to Superior Court under Georgia's process.

The state also allows a written refund request for tax that was assessed and collected in error, starting within three years of payment. A Fayette property return, filed between January 1 and April 1, is how a taxpayer states an opinion of value. Georgia law requires a return in the first full year of ownership, and later returns are needed only when the property changes.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Fayette County property tax?
sections.html:
The commissioner says the county does not sell tax liens or tax lien certificates. It holds one real property sheriff's tax sale each year, and details appear on the Tax Sales tab of the commissioner's site.

If you inherit or buy a Fayette house with back taxes, ask the commissioner for a payoff in writing before closing. Georgia's Department of Revenue notes that delinquent tax can bring penalties as well as interest, and the commissioner reports interest after the delinquent date. A buyer's title company will check for open tax at closing, so a clean payoff speeds things up.

Boats, aircraft and business personal property are taxable in Georgia, and the commissioner says they are taxed in the county where they are located. If a seller keeps a boat docked in another county, that county bills it.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Fayette County housing?
sections.html:
Fayette had 125,156 residents in July 2025, a 5.0 percent gain over the 2020 base of 119,193, the fastest growth among the three counties in the same Census table. The land area is 194.56 square miles, and the density in 2020 was 612.6 residents per square mile.

  • Housing units in 2025: 47,621.
  • Households: 44,581, at 2.72 persons each.
  • Residents 65 and over: 22.7 percent.
  • Persons in poverty: 5.8 percent.
  • Employer establishments in 2023: 3,995.
  • Total retail sales in 2022: $2,249,924 thousand.

The county government says Fayette began to grow in the 1970s with the expansion of Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, and that it adopted building codes and zoning in 1959 and 1960. That early planning shows in a county of five municipalities that still prizes orderly development.

faqs.q: When do Fayette County property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: After November 15, or 60 days after the bills were mailed, whichever is later. The commissioner's FAQ says bills usually arrive around mid September, and interest accrues after the delinquent date.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Fayette County property tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the Tax Commissioner at (770) 461-3652. The office is at 140 W. Stonewall Avenue, Suite 110, in Fayetteville. The Assessors' Office handles values and does not generate bills.

faqs.q: What is the Fayette County homestead exemption deadline?
faqs.a: Applications must be complete by April 1 to apply to the current tax year. The assessors' page also says applications can be accepted beyond April 1, up to the end of the 45-day window to appeal an assessment notice.

faqs.q: Are Fayette County mobile home taxes due on a different date?
faqs.a: Yes. Mobile home bills are mailed January 1 and are due on or before April 1, with a 10 percent penalty after the due date. New owners must register the home with the Tax Commissioner's Office, and a decal is issued once the tax is paid.

faqs.q: Does Fayette County sell tax liens?
faqs.a: No. The commissioner says the county does not sell tax liens or tax lien certificates. It holds one real property sheriff's tax sale per year.
